confirming.Affected users and systems: Local users of this README-only repository; the affected execution path is a new Python CLI named tally. No existing modules or tests were found.
confirming.Constraints and boundaries: The CLI is strictly read-only, uses Python 3 standard library only, accepts one or more explicit UTF-8 text file paths, and does not read stdin, package, recurse, or modify files. Directories and missing, unreadable, or invalid UTF-8 files produce plain stderr errors and exit 1. Successful output is exactly '<count> <path>' per file in argument order, with no total.
confirming.Downstream handoff: The session folder is the handoff: session/seed-contract.md, ledger.json, seed-confirmation.json, and seed-checks.json. A consumer should use tinkery seed status --json <session>; this is discovery input, not implementation approval.

The settled goal and pre-mortem decision establish Python, explicit files, whitespace-token counting, exact output, errors, exit codes, read-only behavior, and unittest expectations. No test files or runnable regression invocation exist; the implementation owner should add unittest coverage and its invocation. What we have not read: no files beyond README.md were present outside Git metadata. An outside review would ask how paths are rendered and how platform-specific read errors are normalized; those details are not established by the repository.

The owner should also establish the runnable entry point and test invocation without adding packaging or recursive traversal.
confirming.Problem statement: The repository currently contains only a README describing tally; the tool is not built yet. Local users need a small, predictable CLI that counts whitespace-separated words in explicitly named text files and reports one result per file.
confirming.Proposed outcome: Add a minimal Python 3 standard-library CLI that reads each named UTF-8 file with str.split(), prints exactly '<count> <path>' in argument order, remains read-only, and reports specified invalid-input cases on stderr with exit 1. Success exits 0.
confirming.Risks and verification: Risks include mutating inputs, counting with rules other than whitespace splitting, changing argument order, accepting directories, mishandling invalid UTF-8, or emitting extra totals or output. Mitigate with temporary-file unittest cases that assert counts, exact stdout/stderr, exit codes, argument order, and unchanged input bytes. These are proposed checks, not completed verification. Where we did not look: no implementation, test suite, CI configuration, packaging metadata, or executable wrapper existed to inspect.
confirming.Suggested first slice: Proposal only: add the smallest Python CLI entry point and its argument/error handling, then verify the behavior with temporary-file unittest cases. The exact executable path and first runnable command are not established by the repository.
